narrative:
The model estimates a 30% chance that you will fail your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your chances of passing.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. The single most important factor is that you have indicated you do not want to pursue higher education. Among students who passed, every single one said they did want to continue studying after school; your answer therefore pulls the prediction strongly toward failure. The second most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. This actually works in your favor and pushes the model toward thinking you will pass. The third notable influence is that you spend relatively little time going out with friends. This also leans slightly toward a passing outcome, since students who go out less tend to have more time available for schoolwork.

Taken together, the lack of ambition for further education outweighs the positive signals from having a clean failure record and lower social outings, leading the model to conclude you are at real risk.

To improve, you should seriously reflect on why you no longer want to continue studying and whether that view could change. Setting clearer goals for after school, combined with keeping your current good habits around study time and low absences, would likely raise your chances considerably.
